# BSPLightmapColor <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [BSP](Blitz3D-BSP)

</div>


```blitzbasic
BSPLightmapColor:Void bsp:Int32, red:Float32, green:Float32, blue:Float32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bsp` | In | Int32 | required | The level. |
| `red` | In | Float32 | required | Red part, 0 to 255. |
| `green` | In | Float32 | required | Green part, 0 to 255. |
| `blue` | In | Float32 | required | Blue part, 0 to 255. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Sets a color that the whole level is multiplied with. This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the original has no such command. A new level starts at 255, 255, 255, which leaves it as it is, and smaller values tint and darken it, down to black for 0, 0, 0. It works with lightmaps and with vertex lighting alike. To brighten a level instead, use [BSPAmbientLight](BSPAmbientLight).
